passage.title: The Ant and the Mandarin
paragraphs: In 1476, the farmers of Berne in Switzerland decided there was only one way to rid their fields of the cutworms attacking their crops. They took the pests to court. The worms were tried, found guilty and excommunicated by the archbishop. In China, farmers had a more practical approach to pest control. Rather than relying on divine intervention, they put their faith in frogs, ducks and ants. Frogs and ducks were encouraged to snap up the pests in the paddies and the occasional plague of locusts. But the notion of biological control began with an ant. More specifically, it started with the predatory yellow citrus ant Oeco-phylla smaragdina, which has been polishing off pests in the orange groves of southern China for at least 1,700 years. The yellow citrus ant is a type of weaver ant, which binds leaves and twigs with silk to form a neat, tent-like nest. In the beginning, farmers made do with the odd ants' nests here and there. But it wasn't long before growing demand led to the development of a thriving trade in nests and a new type of agriculture - ant farming.

For an insect that bites, the yellow citrus ant is remarkably popular. Even by ant standards, Oecophylla smaragdina is a fearsome predator. It's big, runs fast and has a powerful nip - painful to humans but lethal to many of the insects that plague the orange groves of Guangdong and Guangxi in southern China. And for at least 17 centuries, Chinese orange growers have harnessed these six-legged killing machines to keep their fruit groves healthy and productive.

Citrus fruits evolved in the Far East and the Chinese discovered the delights of their flesh early on. As the ancestral home of oranges, lemons and pomelos, China also has the greatest diversity of citrus pests. And the trees that produce the sweetest fruits, the mandarins - or kan - attract a host of plant-eating insects, from black ants and sap-sucking mealy bugs to leaf-devouring caterpillars. With so many enemies, fruit growers clearly had to have some way of protecting their orchards.

The West did not discover the Chinese orange growers' secret weapon until the early 20th century. At the time, Florida was suffering an epidemic of citrus canker and in 1915 Walter Swingle, a plant physiologist working for the US Department of Agriculture, was sent to China in search of varieties of orange that were resistant to the disease. Swingle spent some time studying the citrus orchards around Guangzhou, and there he came across the story of the cultivated ant. These ants, he was told, were "grown'' by the people of a small village nearby who sold them to the orange growers by the nestful.

The earliest report of citrus ants at work among the orange trees appeared in a book on tropical and subtropical botany written by Hsi Han in AD 304."The people of Chiao-Chih sell in their markets ants in bags of rush matting. The nests are like silk. The bags are all attached to twigs and leaves which, with the ants inside the nests, are for sale. The ants are reddish-yellow in colour, bigger than ordinary ants. In the south, if the kan trees do not have this kind of ant, the fruits will all be damaged by many harmful insects, and not a single fruit will be perfect."

Initially, farmers relied on nests which they collected from the wild or bought in the market where trade in nests was brisk."It is said that in the south orange trees which are free of ants will have wormy fruits. Therefore, people race to buy nests for their orange trees," wrote Liu Hsun in Strange Things Noted in the South in about 890.

The business quickly became more sophisticated. From the 10th century, country people began to trap ants in artificial nests baited with fat."Fruit-growing families buy these ants from vendors who make a business of collecting and selling such creatures," wrote Chuang Chi-Yu in 1130."They trap them by filling hogs' or sheep's bladders with fat and placing them with the cavities open next to the ants' nests. They wait until the ants have migrated into the bladders and take them away. This is known as 'rearing orange ants'." Farmers attached the bladders to their trees, and in time the ants spread to other trees and built new nests.

By the 17th century, growers were building bamboo walkways between their trees to speed the colonisation of their orchards.
The ants ran along these narrow bridges from one tree to another and established nests "by the hundreds of thousands”.

Did it work? The orange growers clearly thought so. One authority, Chhii Ta-Chun, writing in 1700, stressed how important it was to keep the fruit trees free of insect pests, especially caterpillars."It is essential to eliminate them so that the trees are not injured. But hand labour is not nearly as efficient as ant power..."

Swingle was just as impressed. Yet despite his reports, many Western biologists were sceptical. In the West, the idea of using one insect to destroy another was new and highly controversial. The first breakthrough had come in 1888, when the infant orange industry in California had been saved from extinction by the Australian vedalia beetle. This beetle was the only thing that had made any inroads into the explosion of cottony cushion scale that was threatening to destroy the state's citrus crops. But, as Swingle now knew, California's "first'' was nothing of the sort. The Chinese had been expert in bio-control for many centuries.

The long tradition of ants in the Chinese orchards only began to waver in the 1950s and 1960s with the introduction of powerful organic insecticides. Although most fruit growers switched to chemicals, a few hung onto their ants. Those who abandoned ants in favour of chemicals quickly became disillusioned. As costs soared and pests began to develop resistance to the chemicals, growers began to revive the old ant patrols in the late 1960s. They had good reason to have faith in their insect workforce.

Research in the early 1960s showed that as long as there were enough ants in the trees, they did an excellent job of dispatching some pests - mainly the larger insects - and had modest success against others. Trees with yellow ants produced almost 20 per cent more healthy leaves than those without. More recent trials have shown that these trees yield just as big a crop as those protected by expensive chemical sprays.

One apparent drawback of using ants - and one of the main reasons for the early scepticism by Western scientists - was that citrus ants do nothing to control mealy bugs, waxy-coated scale insects which can do considerable damage to fruit trees. In fact, the ants protect mealy bugs in exchange for the sweet honey-dew they secrete. The orange growers always denied this was a problem but Western scientists thought they knew better.

Research in the 1980s suggests that the growers were right all along. Where mealy bugs proliferate under the ants' protection, they are usually heavily parasitised and this limits the harm they can do.

Orange growers who rely on carnivorous ants rather than poisonous chemicals maintain a better balance of species in their orchards. While the ants deal with the bigger insect pests, other predatory species keep down the numbers of smaller pests such as scale insects and aphids. In the long run, ants do a lot less damage than chemicals - and they're certainly more effective than excommunication.

question_groups.instructions: Look at the following events and the list of dates below. Match each event with the correct time.
question_groups.body:
The first description of citrus ants is traded in the marketplace. ____ (14)
Swingle came to Asia for research. ____ (15)
The first record of one insect is used to tackle other insects in the western world. ____ (16)
Chinese fruit growers started to use pesticides in place of citrus ants. ____ (17)
Some Chinese farmers returned to the traditional bio-method. ____ (18)
question_groups.body_html:
1. The first description of citrus ants is traded in the marketplace. [14]
  2. Swingle came to Asia for research. [15]
  3. The first record of one insect is used to tackle other insects in the western world. [16]
  4. Chinese fruit growers started to use pesticides in place of citrus ants. [17]
  5. Some Chinese farmers returned to the traditional bio-method. [18]

questions.text: The first description of citrus ants is traded in the marketplace.
questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:
Mô tả đầu tiên về việc kiến vàng được giao dịch trên thị trường.

Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
• first description ~ earliest report
• traded in the marketplace ~ sell in their markets
• citrus ants ~ từ khóa giữ nguyên

Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ: "Báo cáo sớm nhất về kiến vàng làm việc giữa các cây cam xuất hiện trong một cuốn sách... viết bởi Hsi Han vào năm AD 304. 'Người dân Giao Chỉ bán trong chợ của họ những con kiến trong túi bện bằng cỏ...'" (The earliest report of citrus ants... written by Hsi Han in AD 304. "The people of Chiao-Chih sell in their markets ants in bags...").
==> Năm AD 304 tương ứng với đáp án C.

Bước 4: Đáp án: C
quotes: The earliest report of citrus ants at work among the orange trees appeared in a book on tropical and subtropical botany written by Hsi Han in AD 304.

questions.text: Swingle came to Asia for research.
questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:
Swingle đến Châu Á để nghiên cứu.

Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
• Swingle ~ từ khóa giữ nguyên
• came to Asia ~ was sent to China
• research ~ in search of / studying

Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ: "Vào thời điểm đó... và vào năm 1915, Walter Swingle... được cử đến Trung Quốc để tìm kiếm các giống cam kháng bệnh" (...and in 1915 Walter Swingle... was sent to China in search of varieties of orange...).
==> Năm 1915 tương ứng với đáp án F.

Bước 4: Đáp án: F
quotes: At the time, Florida was suffering an epidemic of citrus canker and in 1915 Walter Swingle, a plant physiologist working for the US Department of Agriculture, was sent to China in search of varieties of orange that were resistant to the disease.

questions.text: The first record of one insect is used to tackle other insects in the western world.
questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:
Ghi chép đầu tiên về việc một loài côn trùng được dùng để đối phó với loài khác ở thế giới phương Tây.

Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
• first record ~ first breakthrough
• western world ~ California (thuộc Mỹ - phương Tây)
• one insect used to tackle other insects ~ orange industry... saved... by the Australian vedalia beetle

Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ: "Bước đột phá đầu tiên đến vào năm 1888, khi ngành công nghiệp cam non trẻ ở California được cứu khỏi sự tuyệt chủng bởi loài bọ rùa vedalia của ÚC" (The first breakthrough had come in 1888, when the infant orange industry in California had been saved from extinction by the Australian vedalia beetle.).
==> Năm 1888 tương ứng với đáp án A.

Bước 4: Đáp án: A
quotes: The first breakthrough had come in 1888, when the infant orange industry in California had been saved from extinction by the Australian vedalia beetle.

questions.text: Chinese fruit growers started to use pesticides in place of citrus ants.
questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:
Nông dân trồng trái cây Trung Quốc bắt đầu sử dụng thuốc trừ sâu thay thế cho kiến vàng.

Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
• pesticides ~ powerful organic insecticides / chemicals
• citrus ants ~ từ khóa giữ nguyên

Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ: "Truyền thống lâu đời nuôi kiến trong các vườn cây ăn quả ở Trung Quốc chỉ bắt đầu lung lay vào những năm 1950 và 1960 với sự ra đời của các loại thuốc trừ sâu hữu cơ mạnh" (The long tradition of ants in the Chinese orchards only began to waver in the 1950s and 1960s with the introduction of powerful organic insecticides.).
==> Thập niên 1950 tương ứng với đáp án D.

Bước 4: Đáp án: D
quotes: The long tradition of ants in the Chinese orchards only began to waver in the 1950s and 1960s with the introduction of powerful organic insecticides.

questions.text: Some Chinese farmers returned to the traditional bio-method.
questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:
Một số nông dân Trung Quốc quay trở lại phương pháp sinh học truyền thống.

Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
• returned to ~ revive
• traditional bio-method ~ old ant patrols
• Some Chinese farmers ~ growers

Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ: "Khi chi phí tăng vọt và sâu bệnh bắt đầu phát triển khả năng kháng hóa chất, những người trồng trọt bắt đầu hồi sinh các đội tuần tra kiến cũ vào cuối những năm 1960" (...growers began to revive the old ant patrols in the late 1960s.).
==> Thập niên 1960 tương ứng với đáp án E.

Bước 4: Đáp án: E
quotes: As costs soared and pests began to develop resistance to the chemicals, growers began to revive the old ant patrols in the late 1960s.

question_groups.instructions:
Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 2?
Write
TRUE if the statement agrees with the information,
FALSE if the statement contradicts the information, or
NOT GIVEN if there is no information on this.

questions.text: China has more citrus pests than any other country in the world.
questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:
Câu hỏi khẳng định về số lượng sâu bệnh (more pests) của Trung Quốc là đứng đầu thế giới (than any other country).

Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
• China ~ từ khóa giữ nguyên
• citrus pests ~ từ khóa giữ nguyên
• has more citrus pests than any other country in the world ⁓ greatest diversity

Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ: "As the ancestral home of oranges, lemons and pomelos, China also has the greatest diversity of citrus pests."
(Là quê hương tổ tiên của cam, chanh và bưởi, Trung Quốc cũng có sự đa dạng lớn nhất về các loài gây hại cây có múi.)
==> Điều này đồng nghĩa với thông tin trong câu hỏi "Trung Quốc có nhiều loài gây hại... hơn bất kỳ quốc gia nào khác" (vì "greatest diversity" nghĩa là đa dạng nhất/nhiều loại nhất)

Bước 4: Đáp án: TRUE
quotes: As the ancestral home of oranges, lemons and pomelos, China also has the greatest diversity of citrus pests.

questions.text: Swingle came to China to search for an insect to bring back to the US.
questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:
Swingle đến Trung Quốc để tìm kiếm một loài côn trùng mang về Mỹ.

Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
• Swingle ~ từ khóa giữ nguyên
• search for an insect ~ search of varieties of orange
• bring back to the US ~ working for the US Department of Agriculture

Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ: "vào năm 1915 Walter Swingle... được cử đến Trung Quốc để tìm kiếm các giống cam kháng bệnh".
==> Điều này trái ngược với thông tin trong câu hỏi "tìm kiếm một loài côn trùng" (Swingle đi tìm giống cam, còn chuyện về kiến là ông tình cờ phát hiện sau đó) (...Swingle... was sent to China in search of varieties of orange that were resistant to the disease.).

Bước 4: Đáp án: FALSE
quotes: At the time, Florida was suffering an epidemic of citrus canker and in 1915 Walter Swingle, a plant physiologist working for the US Department of Agriculture, was sent to China in search of varieties of orange that were resistant to the disease.

questions.text: Many people were very impressed by Swingle's discovery.
questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:
Nhiều người đã rất ấn tượng với khám phá của Swingle.

Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
• Many people ~ many Western biologists
• impressed ~ từ khóa giữ nguyên
• Swingle's discovery ~ his reports

Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ: "Swingle cũng ấn tượng không kém. Tuy nhiên, bất chấp các báo cáo của ông, nhiều nhà sinh vật học phương Tây vẫn hoài nghi".
==> Điều này trái ngược với thông tin trong câu hỏi "nhiều người đã rất ấn tượng" (thực tế họ hoài nghi - sceptical) (Yet despite his reports, many Western biologists were sceptical.).

Bước 4: Đáp án: FALSE
quotes: Yet despite his reports, many Western biologists were sceptical.

questions.text: Chinese farmers found that pesticides became increasingly expensive.
questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:
Nông dân Trung Quốc thấy rằng thuốc trừ sâu ngày càng trở nên đắt đỏ.

Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
• pesticides ~ chemicals
• increasingly expensive ~ costs soared

Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ: "Những người bỏ kiến để chuyển sang hóa chất đã nhanh chóng vỡ mộng. Khi chi phí tăng vọt...".
==> Điều này đồng nghĩa với thông tin trong câu hỏi "thuốc trừ sâu ngày càng trở nên đắt đỏ" (Those who abandoned ants in favour of chemicals quickly became disillusioned. As costs soared...).

Bước 4: Đáp án: TRUE
quotes: As costs soared and pests began to develop resistance to the chemicals, growers began to revive the old ant patrols in the late 1960s.

questions.text: Some Chinese farmers abandoned the use of pesticide.
questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:
Một số nông dân Trung Quốc đã từ bỏ việc sử dụng thuốc trừ sâu.

Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
• abandoned ~ revive the old ant patrols
• use of pesticide ~ chemicals

Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ: "những người trồng trọt bắt đầu hồi sinh các đội tuần tra kiến cũ vào cuối những năm 1960".
==> Điều này đồng nghĩa với thông tin trong câu hỏi "một số nông dân đã từ bỏ sử dụng thuốc trừ sâu" để quay lại dùng kiến (...growers began to revive the old ant patrols in the late 1960s.).

Bước 4: Đáp án: TRUE
quotes: As costs soared and pests began to develop resistance to the chemicals, growers began to revive the old ant patrols in the late 1960s.

questions.text: Trees with ants had more leaves fall than those without.
questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:
Những cây có kiến có nhiều lá rụng hơn những cây không có kiến.

Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
• Trees with ants ~ Trees with yellow ants
• more leaves fall ~ produced... more healthy leaves

Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ: "Cây có kiến vàng tạo ra nhiều hơn gần 20% lá khỏe mạnh so với những cây không có".
==> Điều này trái ngược với thông tin trong câu hỏi "có nhiều lá rụng hơn" (nhiều lá khỏe mạnh hơn đồng nghĩa với việc ít rụng hơn hoặc tình trạng cây tốt hơn) (Trees with yellow ants produced almost 20 per cent more healthy leaves than those without.).

Bước 4: Đáp án: FALSE
quotes: Trees with yellow ants produced almost 20 per cent more healthy leaves than those without.

questions.text: Fields using ants yield as large a crop as fields using chemical pesticides.
questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:
Các cánh đồng sử dụng kiến cho năng suất cây trồng lớn bằng các cánh đồng sử dụng thuốc trừ sâu hóa học.

Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
• yield as large a crop ~ yield just as big a crop
• chemical pesticides ~ expensive chemical sprays

Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ: "Các thử nghiệm gần đây hơn đã chỉ ra rằng những cây này mang lại sản lượng lớn tương đương với những cây được bảo vệ bằng các loại thuốc xịt hóa học đắt tiền".
==> Điều này đồng nghĩa với thông tin trong câu hỏi "cho năng suất lớn bằng" (More recent trials have shown that these trees yield just as big a crop as those protected by expensive chemical sprays.).

Bước 4: Đáp án: TRUE
quotes: More recent trials have shown that these trees yield just as big a crop as those protected by expensive chemical sprays.

questions.text: Citrus ants often cause considerable damage to the bio-environment of the orchards.
questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:
Kiến vàng thường gây ra thiệt hại đáng kể cho môi trường sinh thái của vườn cây.

Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
• cause considerable damage ~ do a lot less damage
• bio-environment of the orchards ~ balance of species in their orchards

Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ: "Về lâu dài, kiến gây ra ít thiệt hại hơn nhiều so với hóa chất".
==> Điều này trái ngược với thông tin trong câu hỏi "gây ra thiệt hại đáng kể" (In the long run, ants do a lot less damage than chemicals...).

Bước 4: Đáp án: FALSE
quotes: Orange growers who rely on carnivorous ants rather than poisonous chemicals maintain a better balance of species in their orchards. While the ants deal with the bigger insect pests, other predatory species keep down the numbers of smaller pests such as scale insects and aphids. In the long run, ants do a lot less damage than chemicals - and they're certainly more effective than excommunication.
